item.description: A tragic stampede occurred at the Chorbagan Durga Puja pandal in north Kolkata on Saturday evening. This incident was triggered by a sudden crowd surge as rain fell, causing panic among waiting devotees. Eyewitnesses reported numerous people losing consciousness and being carried away for medical assistance. Authorities, including police and disaster management teams, have been deployed to assist the injured.

item.title: Goodwill listed gold Lego piece from $14.95; rare mask later sold for $18,101
item.description: A small gold LEGO mask found inside a donated jewellery bag at a Goodwill store in Pennsylvania turned out to be a rare collector's item. Initially listed for $14.95, the 14-karat gold Bionicle Kanohi Hau mask attracted bids from collectors and eventually sold for $18,101 in March 2024. Only 30 such masks were produced in 2001.

item.title: Muhammad Ali’s former training camp restored for $1m and reopened as museum
item.description: Mike Madden's dedication to preserving sports history shines brightly as he invests $1.5 million into restoring Fighter's Heaven, the legendary training camp originally founded by Muhammad Ali in 1972. After years of neglect, the camp reopened to an enthusiastic public in June 2019, earning praise from Pennsylvania’s State Historic Preservation Office for its cultural importance.

item.title: USCIS: Anyone who ‘guarantees’ a faster visa or Green Card is scamming you
item.description: USCIS warns immigrants and visa applicants about fraudulent schemes that promise quicker visa approvals in exchange for monetary fees. These scams frequently involve false claims of having special ties to government officials. USCIS insists that no one can hasten the immigration process through personal connections. Individuals should file applications independently and trust assistance only from recognized professionals. Recognizing fraudulent emails and suspicious offers is essential to protect against these scams.

item.title: 1923 Australian church turned three-bedroom home now lists up to $950,000
item.description: Nestled in Tyabb, Victoria, a stunning transformation has taken place as a historic 1923 Methodist church is now a three-bedroom haven ready for new owners. This charming residence boasts impressive cathedral ceilings, original windows, and contemporary kitchen features. Perfect for hosting, it includes a spacious living area and a dedicated bedroom wing, all while preserving a landmark rich in history—including its past as a Sunday school and dance venue.

item.title: Tiger Woods’ children Sam and Charlie: How are they shaping his golf legacy?
item.description: Tiger Woods allows his children to pursue their own interests and dreams. But has also left the door open for them to play golf. Sam has been at Stanford University, while Charlie has taken up competitive golf and signed with Florida State University, and their divergent paths underscore the lasting legacy of the Woods family beyond Tiger’s legendary career.

item.description: A tragic stampede at a Durga Puja pandal in Kolkata has claimed the lives of at least 17 people. The chaos was reportedly caused by severe rain and a massive influx of attendees. Eyewitnesses recounted scenes of distress, with numerous individuals fainting under the circumstances. Emergency services acted quickly, transporting the seriously injured to Calcutta Medical College.

Emergency services transported the injured to Calcutta Medical College and Hospital for immediate medical assistance. The West Bengal health minister, alongside other political leaders, responded by visiting the scene and the hospital.

item.title: Why Trump's plan to unleash 'Mother Of All Bombs' may fall flat in Iran
item.description: Military discussions are considering the use of the MOAB against Iran's nuclear facilities and military targets. However, the effectiveness of the MOAB is limited against deeply buried sites protected by reinforced concrete. Analysts highlight that the GBU-57 penetrator is better suited for such underground facilities, which require specialized weapons for effective targeting. While the MOAB has a strong psychological impact, its military utility against hardened targets is questionable.
item.dc:creator: DHRUV YADAV

item.title: Rain washes out series decider after India script history vs West Indies
item.description: In a remarkable display, India achieved the quickest team fifty in men's T20I cricket, accomplishing this feat in a mere 2.5 overs against the West Indies. Unfortunately, relentless rain led to the abandonment of the match. The series concluded with both teams even at 2-2 after five thrilling encounters, with India's swift scoring and the record-setting fifty marking a high point in the series finale.

item.title: '9 murders' claim, then clarification: How 'Chhote Sarkar' put Nitish on the spot
item.description: Anant Singh is no ordinary legislator as locals rarely use his given name. They call him 'Chhote Sarkar', or little lord, because in the Barh and Mokama belt his word has often counted for more than the government’s. His story begins with his elder brother, Dilip Singh, who won as an independent and became a minister in Lalu Prasad’s cabinet during its first term, from 1990 to 1995.

item.title: UP man strangles sister with dupatta after finding man in her room at 3.30am
item.description: Ashish Kumar allegedly strangled his sister Komal to death after discovering a young man in her room. This incident occurred on October 16 at their home in Lakhanor village. Following a complaint made by the victim's uncle, police arrested Kumar on the same day. During interrogation, Kumar admitted to killing Komal during an argument over the situation. He was later produced in court after completing all necessary legal procedures.

item.title: Bhuvneshwar Kumar makes India comeback after four years

Captain Shreyas Iyer has included Bhuvneshwar along with Shivam Dube in the playing XI. West Indies leader Shai Hope opted for a bowling-first strategy, hoping to leverage it to his team's advantage.

item.title: SC’s enquiry committee launches complaint portal over violence during July protests
item.description: A complaint portal has been launched by the High Powered Enquiry Committee for individuals affected by protests. This portal allows victims to confidentially submit their complaints regarding violence that occurred in July. The Ministry of Home Affairs stated that submissions can also be made in person or via post. The committee will prioritize cases involving serious violence, especially against women protesters.

item.title: 'Can't die like this': Indian pilot Smit Machchhar recalls flydubai flight ordeal
item.description: In a shocking incident on September 30, Indian Captain Smit Machchhar endured an assault by his Omani co-pilot aboard flydubai flight FZ1073 en route from Dubai to Tel Aviv. With injury and determination, Machchhar opened the cockpit door, allowing passengers to step in and restrain the assailant. The aircraft landed safely in Tabuk, Saudi Arabia, following a critical altitude drop.

item.title: 'Can't believe he's not first choice': Clarke slams India over Kuldeep snub
item.description: The recent decision by India to omit Kuldeep Yadav from the T20I squad has ignited discussions among cricket analysts. Experts like Michael Clarke emphasize that Kuldeep's knack for claiming wickets is invaluable in T20 matches. Meanwhile, Naman Dhir has adequately taken on the role of the second spinner. Nevertheless, Kuldeep's past performances against the West Indies, along with his extensive experience, raise important questions about India's future selection policies.

item.title: 'Arbitrary, unreasonable’: Actor Imran Khan moves HC to challenge 'leave India' notice
item.description: Imran Khan Pal filed a petition against a notice mandating his departure from India by October 28. He claims the notice violates his fundamental rights under the Indian Constitution and lacks justification. Khan argues that he has lived in India since he was two years old and is an Overseas Citizen of India. The notice was issued following his attendance at a protest, leading to claims of arbitrary detention.
